The one non-idiomatic seam is the reliance on an internal build-render hostname, plus a hand-rolled fragment-fetch layer where the (experimental) page-premises mechanism exists.

review_cost.rationale: Approve after a nits pass: dead exports, cache eviction, per-island aborting, and an error path for API failures. Nothing requires rearchitecting.

findings.issue: A single module-global AbortController is shared by pokemon-browser, moves-panel and team-page; any two in-flight fragment fetches abort each other. It only works today because no page has two fetching islands.
findings.suggestion: Give each island (or each selector) its own controller, e.g. a small Map keyed by the fragment selector, or pass the controller in from the caller.

findings.issue: isBuildRender compares url.hostname to the undocumented internal stub host 'gracile-static'. If a Gracile release changes the build-render URL, every route silently starts fetching API data at build time, breaking the 'no build-time data' requirement and the build itself.
findings.suggestion: Keep the check but defend it: also treat empty params (the build context passes params: {}) or a dedicated env/flag as build renders, and assert the hostname in a comment with a link to the framework source so it is re-verified on upgrades.

findings.issue: apiRequired throws when a resource is missing and nothing catches it: a single failed or non-OK API response turns any page into an unhandled rejection and a framework 500 page, with no retry or degradation.
findings.suggestion: Wrap route loads (or the api() transport) so a failed sub-resource degrades — render the sections that did load, or fall back to a styled error/404 page instead of the raw framework error.

findings.issue: The TTL cache only skips expired entries; it never removes them, so the Map grows monotonically with every distinct API URL requested over the server's lifetime.
findings.suggestion: Purge expired entries opportunistically (e.g. when a lookup misses, or cap the Map size with an LRU).

findings.issue: The debounce timer set by 'input' is not cleared on 'change', so changing a select fires an extra, redundant fragment fetch 150 ms later; the window 'popstate' listener is also never removed in disconnectedCallback.
findings.suggestion: clearTimeout(this.#timer) at the top of the change handler, and add a disconnectedCallback that removes the popstate listener.

findings.issue: Removing a team member replaces the entire <team-page> subtree — including the h1 and the '<n> of 6' text — which can disturb scroll and focus if the user was focused elsewhere in the page.
findings.suggestion: Refresh only the card list and coverage section (give them ids and swap those nodes), leaving the page chrome intact.

findings.issue: toggleTeamMember is dead code — team-toggle.ts implements its own toggle logic inline and nothing imports it.
findings.suggestion: Delete it, or have team-toggle use it so the team mutation rules live in exactly one place.

findings.issue: moveTables is exported from the route module but only used inside it, adding a stray public surface to a file whose default export is the route.
findings.suggestion: Drop the export keyword; the template partial belongs next to the route that renders it.

findings.issue: Asset hrefs are built with new URL('./styles/app.css', import.meta.url).pathname — it works (Gracile's html-routes build rewrites them) but differs from the documented plain '/src/...' form and yields OS-dependent path separators in principle.
findings.suggestion: Use plain root-relative source paths like the framework's own document example, and let the build pipeline do the resolving.

summary: This is a disciplined, genuinely idiomatic Gracile app: the route/document/island structure mirrors the framework's own examples, the server–client boundary is clean, and the shared partials and helpers make it easy to read. The concerns are robustness rather than structure — a shared global abort controller, an undocumented build-render hostname the whole app depends on, an append-only cache, and no error path for API failures. I would merge after a nits pass fixing those and removing the dead exports.
